title: Fast Evaluation of the Sixth-Order Time-Convolutionless Master-Equation Generator and Beyond
authors: Jiahao Chen, Sirui Chen, Dragomir Davidovic
abstract: Direct quadrature of the Hadamard-reduced sixth-order time-convolutionless (TCL6) generator at all $N_t$ sampled times requires $O(N_t^3)$ operations at fixed system dimension. We derive an exact reduction for a finite-dimensional system coupled through one Hermitian operator to a stationary centered Gaussian bath. By separating fixed operator coefficients from scalar bath kernels, the complete TCL6 time series is reduced to cumulative sums and first-order recurrences, one-dimensional causal convolutions, and an exact dyadic recursion for interlocked histories. With the algorithm, evaluating the complete TCL6 time series requires $O(N_t\log^2 N_t)$ operations at fixed system dimension. In addition, we show that TCL$2n$ can be evaluated with $O(N_t\log^{n-1} N_t)$ complexity. A fixed finite Matsubara expansion of the bath correlation function permits $O(N_t\log N_t)$ evaluation at any fixed TCL order. These reductions enable fast long-time simulations of non-Markovian open quantum systems within the regime of validity of the TCL expansion.
summary: This paper presents an advanced mathematical technique to drastically speed up the calculation of the sixth-order time-convolutionless master-equation generator. By decomposing complex time integrals into simpler components solvable by convolutions and recurrences, the computational scaling is improved from cubic to near-linear in the number of time steps. This enables long-time simulations of complex, non-Markovian quantum dynamics.
main_problem: The paper addresses the computational bottleneck associated with directly evaluating the high-order (sixth-order) time-convolutionless (TCL6) master-equation generator for open quantum systems.
main_result: A novel algorithmic reduction is derived that lowers the computational complexity from $O(N_t^3)$ to $O(N_t \log^2 N_t)$ for the TCL6 time series evaluation.
method: The core method involves mathematically separating the time-dependent bath correlation functions into independent, joined, and interlocked history components, allowing for evaluation via cumulative sums, convolutions, and specialized recurrences.
model_or_system: The system is a fixed finite-dimensional quantum system coupled to a stationary centered Gaussian bath via a single Hermitian operator. The dynamics are governed by the time-local generator derived from the TCL expansion.
key_observables: The complete TCL6 time series, $K_I(t)$, and its matrix elements $S_{6,k}$.
important_parameters: The time step count ($N_t$), the order of the expansion (e.g., TCL6, $	ext{TCL}_{2n}$), and the history-coupling depth ($\ell_H$).
main_assumptions: The reduction relies on the system coupling through a single Hermitian operator to a Gaussian bath, and the complexity analysis assumes the availability of specific reduction identities.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the overall reduction process from commutators to evaluating scalar sums. Figure 2 details the recursive structure used for the interlocked-history contraction.
paper_structure: The paper systematically moves from the general definition of the TCL6 generator to deriving an exact reduction by separating fixed operator coefficients from scalar bath kernels, which are then evaluated using cumulative sums, FFT convolutions, and specialized dyadic recursions for interlocked histories.
why_interesting: This work provides a significant algorithmic breakthrough for simulating non-Markovian dynamics, which is crucial for understanding open quantum systems where memory effects are dominant.
